security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, and TSX examples. Confirmed issues are limited to documented npx install commands, a remote component registry URL, and a remote image that can trigger a network request when rendered. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the shadcn CLI version, document the registry source, and advise users to inspect downloaded components before installation.
Mark related npx skills add commands as optional and recommend reviewing each referenced skill before installation.
Host the image through the marketplace or include a local asset to avoid third-party requests during page render.

content.value_statement: Agent applications need clear status views for tool calls, approvals, and results. This skill shows how to add React and Next.js components from ui.inference.sh for that workflow.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install tool UI components with shadcn.
Explains pending, running, approval, success, and error tool states.
Provides React examples for ToolCall, ToolResult, and ToolApproval components.
Demonstrates approval callbacks for human review before tool execution.
Maps common tool name patterns to visual icons.
Shows integration with an Agent component and a proxy route.
limitations: The skill is documentation only and does not include component source files.
Examples depend on external ui.inference.sh component registry availability.
It does not implement backend tool execution or authorization logic.
It assumes a React or Next.js project using shadcn-style components.

use_cases.title: Add Tool Status Views
use_cases.description: Frontend engineers can display pending, running, success, and error states for agent tools.

use_cases.title: Review Sensitive Actions
use_cases.description: AI product teams can add approval UI before tools send messages, write files, or call services.

use_cases.title: Prototype Agent Interfaces
use_cases.description: Prototype builders can combine tool calls, results, and approvals in a Next.js agent interface.

prompt_templates.title: Show Basic Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a simple ToolCall display for a running search_web tool in my React app. Follow the tools-ui guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Add Approval Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ToolApproval view for a send_email tool. Include approve and deny callbacks and clear argument display.

prompt_templates.title: Render Mixed Tool Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tool activity panel that shows pending calls, successful results, and errors using the tools-ui components.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate With Agent Runtime
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect the tools-ui components to my Agent configuration. Include approval gates for web search and file write tools.

output_examples.input: Request: Show a running web search tool.
output_examples.output: A compact tool card named search_web shows the running status, query details, and a progress indicator.

output_examples.input: Request: Add approval before sending email.
output_examples.output: An approval panel displays recipient and subject, with approve and deny actions tied to tool lifecycle callbacks.
A result block labels the tool name, marks the action as successful, and summarizes returned content.

best_practices: Use approval UI for tools that send data, modify files, or contact external services.
Keep tool arguments readable and mask sensitive values before display.
Match tool states from your runtime to the documented status names.
anti_patterns: Do not show raw sensitive arguments such as tokens, secrets, or private messages.
Do not treat the UI approval as backend authorization.
Do not run installation commands without reviewing the remote registry source.

faq.question: Does this skill install components automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and examples. A user or agent must run installation steps explicitly.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it target?
faq.answer: It targets React and Next.js projects using shadcn-style component workflows.

faq.question: Can it execute tools?
faq.answer: No. It displays tool lifecycle states and approval controls. Backend execution remains in your application.

faq.question: Does it support approval gates?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include a ToolApproval component with approve and deny callbacks.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that surface tool calls.

faq.question: What should I review before use?
faq.answer: Review remote installation commands, component source, and any displayed tool arguments for sensitive data.
